title: Security of Quantum Conference Key Agreement with Two-Way Classical Communication
authors: Shun Kawakami, Mori Watanabe, Takuya Ikuta, Koichi Takasugi
abstract: Quantum conference key agreement (QCKA) enables multiple users to establish a common secret key with information-theoretic security and is regarded as a key primitive for secure communication in future quantum networks. However, practical implementations of QCKA typically suffer from higher noise levels than conventional bipartite quantum key distribution (QKD), making the improvement of the tolerable error threshold an important challenge. Gottesman and Lo proposed two preprocessing procedures for QKD with two-way classical communication, known as the B-step and the P-step, which enhance the tolerable error threshold. In this paper, we analyze the asymptotic security of QCKA with tripartite GHZ states and two measurement bases using two-way classical communication, including multiple B-steps and P-steps. We derive the corresponding secure key rate analytically and demonstrate that iterative B-steps can increase the tolerable error threshold beyond 20%, significantly improving upon the approximately 11% threshold achievable without two-way classical communication and the approximately 15% threshold obtained with only a single B-step. Our results show that two-way classical communication can substantially enhance the robustness of practical QCKA protocols.
summary: This paper enhances the security analysis of Quantum Conference Key Agreement (QCKA) using GHZ states. By incorporating multiple rounds of two-way classical communication steps (B-steps and P-steps), the authors analytically prove that the tolerable error threshold can be substantially increased beyond previous limits. This work is crucial for realizing robust, practical quantum networks.
main_problem: The paper analyzes the asymptotic security of Quantum Conference Key Agreement (QCKA) for multiple users, focusing on improving the tolerable error threshold in practical implementations.
main_result: Iterative application of two-way classical communication steps (B-steps and P-steps) can increase the tolerable error threshold beyond 20%, significantly enhancing protocol robustness.
method: The authors derive the secure key rate analytically by optimizing over physically realizable error rates, incorporating iterative updates for parameter estimation.
model_or_system: The system models QCKA using tripartite Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger (GHZ) states and two complementary measurement bases (Z and X). The security analysis is asymptotic ($N 	o \infty$).
key_observables: Secure key rate ($R$), error rates ($s_1, s_2, s_3, s_4$, etc.), and the tolerable error threshold.
important_parameters: The optimization involves maximizing over multiple interconnected error parameters subject to physical constraints defining a realizable parameter space.
main_assumptions: Assumes IID eavesdropping interaction; the analysis is asymptotic; specific bounds on error rates ($s_i < 1/2$) are used throughout the derivation.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the security by first establishing the key rate formula, then deriving and optimizing the parameter updates for multiple B-steps and P-steps, and finally verifying that the resulting analytical solutions satisfy all necessary physical constraints across different geometric regimes.
why_interesting: It provides rigorous theoretical advancements in quantum network security protocols, directly impacting the feasibility of multi-user quantum communication systems by quantifying error tolerance improvements.
